title: Beef Wellington
subtitle: Beef fillet in mushroom duxelles and puff pastry
excerpt: The showstopper of British cooking: a perfectly cooked beef fillet wrapped in a layer of mushroom duxelles and prosciutto, encased in golden puff pastry and baked until the pastry is crisp and the beef is still pink and juicy within.

recipe.sourceNotes: Beef Wellington is a British dish named after the Duke of Wellington, though the origin story may be apocryphal. The dish consists of a whole beef fillet coated in a layer of mushroom duxelles (finely chopped mushrooms cooked until completely dry) and thin slices of prosciutto, then wrapped in puff pastry and baked. The challenge is achieving a perfectly cooked, pink interior with a crisp, evenly browned pastry exterior. The duxelles and prosciutto act as a barrier that prevents the pastry becoming soggy from the meat juices. The fillet must be seared very aggressively and then fully chilled before wrapping; the pastry must also be well chilled before going in the oven. Getting the timing right for a crowd is the main difficulty.

content.text: The fillet must be very well seared all over; this step provides flavour and forms a barrier against moisture. The duxelles must be cooked until completely dry; any residual moisture will make the pastry soggy. Every component should be fully chilled before assembly. Use a meat thermometer: 52°C internal is rare, 57°C is medium-rare, 63°C is medium.

content.text: Make the duxelles: cook the shallots and garlic in butter for 5 minutes. Add the mushrooms and thyme. Cook over high heat, stirring frequently, for 15 to 20 minutes until completely dry with no liquid remaining. Season. Cool completely.

Season and sear the fillet in very hot oil for 2 minutes per side until deeply browned all over, including the ends. Brush all over with Dijon mustard. Cool completely in the fridge. Lay the prosciutto slices overlapping on cling film. Spread the duxelles over the prosciutto. Place the fillet at one edge and roll tightly. Chill for 30 minutes.

Preheat the oven to 220°C / fan 200°C / gas 7. Roll the pastry into a rectangle large enough to wrap the fillet. Unwrap the fillet and place on the pastry. Brush the edges with egg wash. Roll and seal tightly, seam-side down. Brush all over with egg wash, score lightly. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the pastry is golden (52°C internal for rare). Rest 10 minutes before slicing.
